items.title: Claude Fable 5 on Bedrock Requires Sharing Inference Data with Anthropic
items.summary_1line: Using Claude Fable 5 or Mythos 5 on Amazon Bedrock requires opting into provider_data_share, sending prompts and outputs to Anthropic for 30-day retention with human review. Previous Bedrock models kept inference data...
items.editor_note: Access returns on Amazon Bedrock after the suspension — but only via provider_data_share, sending prompts and outputs to Anthropic for 30-day retention with human review, unlike prior Bedrock models.

editorial.tldr: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5 and the unguarded Mythos 5 as long-horizon models "made safe for general use," but a US export-control directive citing national security suspended access days later. The models returned gated on Amazon Bedrock behind a data-sharing opt-in, then redeployed from July 1 once the controls lifted, with Anthropic detailing the cyber classifiers and jailbreak severity framework behind that redeploy two days later.
editorial.whats_new: A builder shipping real code with Fable 5 on a Claude Max subscription says that access is closing within days — the first sign the July 1 redeploy may not hold across every subscription tier.
editorial.why_it_matters: Whether Max-plan access survives is now as material as the classifier details: teams leaning on Fable 5 through a consumer-tier subscription need to know if that path is stable before they build around it.
editorial.take_for_builders: Confirm whether your Fable 5 access path (API, Bedrock, or Max-plan usage) has a firm end date before depending on it further, and keep a fallback model wired in case Max-tier access lapses the way Bedrock access was gated before it.

status.reenable: no official end-of-access notice from Anthropic yet
status.detail: Fable 5 and Mythos 5 launched "made safe for general use," were suspended by a US export-control directive, returned on Amazon Bedrock only under a data-sharing opt-in, redeployed from July 1 with published cyber safeguards, and on July 5 a Claude Max subscriber reported that tier's access to Fable 5 is ending within days.

open_questions: Is the reported end of Fable 5 access on Claude Max subscriptions an official, product-wide change, and what happens to it after?
Does the July 1 redeployment restore standard private-inference terms, or does the Bedrock provider_data_share requirement persist?
Do the published cyber classifiers close the specific jailbreak that triggered the export-control suspension, or does exposure remain?
Will other frontier labs adopt the first-draft jailbreak severity framework, or does it stay Anthropic-only?
Is Fable 5 / Mythos 5 redeploying beyond Bedrock — first-party API or other clouds — on private-inference terms?
